 guide Gensa Editorial Team Nov 21, 2026 Brooklyn Share The holiday season is here, and we’ve compiled a bucket list for families to make the most of it this year in Brooklyn. Go ice skating, check out a light show, eat at a festive restaurant, stay warm at an indoor play space, celebrate at a tree lighting, meet Santa, treat mom to some much needed self care, find a hotel for visiting family, shop local at a holiday market and much more this year!
 Our new Events Calendar is here featuring the most comprehensive list of free events for families. Plus filters by category, location, ages, dates and more to make your Brooklyn social life as fun and meaningful as possible this holiday season. 
 Have you checked out O ur Service Directory – where families find what matters? Whether you are looking for a meal delivery service for the holidays, photographers for holiday photos, self-care for Mom & Dad during the stressful holiday season, pet sitters while you’re traveling, or day camps while school is out. 
 Family-Friendly Holiday Experiences 
 Our overview of family-friendly holiday and winter activities includes free and fee-based experiences in Brooklyn and beyond, including light shows, special dance and circus performances, unique holiday experiences, and more.
 Ad Advertisement Ad Advertisement Give back this holiday season 
 As the holidays approach, there are many ways for Brooklyn families to volunteer time or resources locally, whether donating holiday toys, crafting ornaments, wrapping gifts, delivering holiday meals, and so much more.
 Tree Lightings 
 Ad Advertisement Ad Advertisement Kick off the holiday season with your neighborhood’s tree lighting . Enjoy live performances, seasonal drinks and bites, appearances from Santa, and the thrilling countdown as the lights come alive!
 Meet Santa 
 Santa’s coming to town! Get your camera ready, we’ve rounded up all the spots to find jolly Old Saint Nick across Brooklyn and lower Manhattan this season. Start with Bklyn Holiday-Topia at City Point in Downtown Brooklyn, on select dates from December 5 to 13, with FREE professional portraits with Santa, holiday crafts and more festive fun.
 Holiday Caroling 
 ‘Tis the season for carolers to spread holiday joy! Get your hot cocoa ready, we’ve rounded up all the most festive caroling events happening across Brooklyn this season. Catch one of these holiday performances, or join your neighbors in a sing-along!
 Festive Restaurants 
 Looking for a festive Brooklyn spot bursting with holiday cheer and over-the-top décor? We’ve rounded up the borough’s most festive restaurants and bars, complete with dazzling decorations, cozy bites, and warming cocktails for the season.
 Ice Skating 
 Ice skating season is here, with rinks reopening across Brooklyn and lower Manhattan. Our overview includes opening dates, locations, hours, admission, and skate rental information.
 Holiday Markets 
 Shop for family, friends, or even yourself at one of the festive holiday markets in Brooklyn this year. Our roundup covers locations, dates, times, and highlights, including festive food and drink, family-friendly activities, and appearances from Santa!
 Drop-in Indoor Activities 
 When your apartment feels too small or the weather is too cold, check out our overview of indoor activities in Brooklyn. This guide of nearly 100 indoor spots includes drop-in activities including play spaces, story times, arts and crafts, adventure parks, rock climbing, mini golf, bowling and more for all ages, from babies to teens!
 Day Camps for when schools are closed 
 Need child care over winter break or looking for a unique experience to keep your child busy? These camps are open when public schools are closed, offering programs for children ages 2 to 14. 
 Urgent Cares 
 Feeling sick during the holiday season? Keep handy our helpful overview of urgent care options for kids in Brooklyn and Lower Manhattan, including dedicated pediatric emergency rooms, inpatient pediatric units, and services for all types of urgent care needs, from X-rays to stitches to treatments for colds and other common illnesses.
 Holiday Date Nights 
 Parents’ night out? Yes, please! Call the babysitter, dust off your date-night outfit, and treat yourself to a special holiday evening out, with delicious food, craft cocktails, and uninterrupted conversation. Check out our delicious round up of our favorite bars and restaurants for date nights in Brooklyn.
 Hotels in Brooklyn for family & friends visiting 
 Whether you’re planning a holiday staycation or helping visiting family or friends find accommodations, Brooklyn has a hotel for every vibe—boutique charm, budget-friendly basics, or rooftop-pool luxury. Our guide will help you find the perfect place to stay or recommend for the holiday season.
 Coffee Shops for some quiet time away from the crew 
 Need to get work done over the winter break? Our guide of Brooklyn coffee shops features peaceful, laptop-friendly spots with cozy vibes—perfect for getting things done or unwinding.
 Family-Friendly Restaurants for the holiday season 
 Have family visiting from out of town, meeting up with friends to exchange gifts, or just looking for a kid-friendly holiday meal out? Check out our overview of family-friendly restaurants across Brooklyn, complete with kids menus, high chairs, and lots of space for strollers.
 Bakeries for your festive treats 
 Looking for festive sweets and treats to accompany your holiday meal? Our guide to Brooklyn’s favorite bakeries features not-to-be-missed cookies, pies, cakes, donuts, pastries, and breads, and more, so you can treat yourself this holiday season!
 Chanukah Fun 
 Hanukkah falls between December 4 and 12 this year, and Brooklyn will celebrate the Jewish Festival Lights with eight days of family-friendly events. Check out our roundup of Chanukah events for families , featuring menorah lightings, story times, live performances, arts and crafts, and more!
 Sledding 
 Will Brooklyn get snow this holiday season?! Be prepared for any winter storms that come our way with our sledding guide , featuring hills in Fort Greene Park, Prospect Park, Brooklyn Bridge Park, and beyond.
